sentences.text: The only known species of this dinosaur is Analong chuanjieensis.
In 2008, an exhibition called Lufeng World Dinosaur Valley was constructed around the skeletons.
Two giant sauropod skeletons were discovered in 1995 by Tao Wang while working with the Lufeng Dinosaur Museum.
The fossils were found in the village of A'na and the town of Chuanjie in Lufeng County, Yunnan.
The skeletons remained in situ until 2000, when they were described and named Chuanjiesaurus.
In 2020, Xin-Xin Ren and colleagues re-examined the specimen LFGT LCD9701-1.
Ren and colleagues determined that LFGT LCD9701-1 was distinct enough from the Chuanjiesaurus holotype to warrant a new genus and species, Analong chuanjiensis.
The genus name Analong refers to the village of A'na and the suffix '-long' means 'dragon' in Mandarin.
The specific epithet chuanjieensis refers to the town of Chuanjie where the fossils were found.
Phylogenetic analysis by its describers suggests Analong was the first mamenchisaurid to diverge evolutionarily within the group.
Ren and colleagues originally classified Analong as a basally-branching member of Mamenchisauridae.
Subsequent studies have reaffirmed Analong's classification as a mamenchisaurid.
Analong belongs to the parent group Mamenchisauridae.
Analong lived during the Middle Jurassic, approximately 168 million years ago, in what is now Asia.
Remains of Analong have been found in the Chuanjie Formation in Yunnan Province, China.
Analog lived between 170.9 and 168.2 million years ago during the Bajocian age.
